correctness.rationale: The domination lemma is elementary and exhaustive. The deletion-link cofiber is a simplicial cofibration. Relative faces split into k-1 mutually incomparable branches plus one exceptional face. The branch quotient is the suspension of the union of a boundary sphere with an attached disk whose attaching sphere maps null-homotopically by dimension. This gives the exact wedge without guessing attaching maps. The stated face matching is acyclic by monotonicity of pivot coordinates and down-closed patching; nine cases have independent exact full-Hasse and mod-two boundary-rank checks.

originality.rationale: The first public archived reference proves a sphere result for forests, not this nonchordal family. Taylan treats chordal graphs and cycles, and the 2023 general Alexander dual statement controls homology but does not imply a full homotopy decomposition in mixed dimensions. The known C4 case is explicitly excluded from individual priority claims. The uniform perfect matching and full multipartite homotopy formula are not found in the inspected works or targeted research records. Literature-indexing risks remain.
residual_risks: General unpublished or not-indexed results on the homotopy type of Alexander duals could cover this multipartite formula; publication novelty is best knowledge, not certified global uniqueness.
The exact first-public publication date of the 2005 archived source was taken from its original PDF header, rather than journal issue year.
The formula excludes singleton parts and does not identify equivariant automorphism representations.

value.rationale: Classifies an infinite, natural, nonchordal family with arbitrary part sizes and genuinely mixed-dimensional sphere summands. Complete homotopy type strictly refines already accessible Alexander-dual homological information. The explicit optimal acyclic matching supplies a reusable combinatorial proof, not just finite ranks. Distinct configurations K_{2,3,4} and K_{2,2} illustrate nontrivial dimensions and multiplicities.
